For the heat treatment process, a T6 treatment was applied, involving a double-stage solid solution treatment followed by a double-stage aging treatment

To produce the 205C parent alloy, the induction furnace was utilized for smelting the aluminum alloy, followed by transferring the molten alloy into a holding furnace at a temperature of 740 ◦C. Argon gas blowing was employed for refining purposes, and the alloy underwent a standing treatment for 30 min.
Subsequently, ingots with a diameter of 110 mm were obtained using a continuous casting method.
The obtained ingots were then subjected to the hot extrusion method, resulting in the production of rods with a diameter of φ 9.5 mm.
These rods underwent a meticulous process involving rolling, drawing, ultrasonic cleaning, and chemical passivation.
Ultimately, φ 1.2 mm coiled wires were obtained.

The WA-DED process was carried out using an ABB welding robotic system equipped with a CMT power source, as depicted in Fig. 1a. A single-lane, multi-layer thin-walled component measuring 240 mm × 65 mm × 9 mm was fabricated on a pure aluminum plate with dimensions of 300 mm × 150 mm × 20 mm, as illustrated in Fig. 1b.
The as-deposited (AD) samples underwent solid solution treatment in a muffle furnace (SX2–4-10, ± 1 ◦C) at 520 ◦C for 6 h, followed by treatment at 535 ◦C for 8 h.
